extracted.intended_audience: Users of the SINGULAR computer algebra system (mathematicians / researchers working with singularities and computational algebra)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference documentation for SINGULAR library procedures: their usage signatures, input assumptions, return values, display/print behaviour, options, and noteworthy notes/examples for computing invariants and deformations of singularities.

rubrics_metrics.name: detadj Usage / assumptions / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: detadj(U); U matrix. Assume: U is a square matrix with non zero determinant. Return: The procedure returns a list with at most 2 entries. If U is not a sqaure matrix, the list is empty. If U is a sqaure matrix, then the first entry is the determinant of U. If U is a square matrix and the determinant of U not zero, then the second entry is the adjoint matrix of U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: The procedure displays comments if printlevel>=1. Example provided showing invocation and accessing list entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: invunit Usage / assumptions / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: invunit(u,n); u poly, n int. Assume: The polynomial u is a series unit. Return: The procedure returns the series inverse of u up to order n or a zero polynomial if u is no series unit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: The procedure displays comments if printlevel>=1. Example shows computing truncated series inverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: jacoblift Purpose / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: jacoblift(f); f poly. Assume/Return: The polynomial f in a series ring (local ordering) defines an isolated hypersurface singularity. The procedure returns a list with entries kappa, xi, u of type int, vector, poly such that kappa is minimal with f^kappa in jacob(f), u is a unit, and u*f^kappa=(matrix(jacob(f))*xi)[1,1].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Display: The procedure displays comments if printlevel>=1. Example shows output list structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: monodromyB Purpose / options / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: monodromyB(f[,opt]); f poly, opt int. Assume/Return: The polynomial f in a series ring (local ordering) defines an isolated hypersurface singularity. The procedure returns a residue matrix M of the meromorphic Gauss-Manin connection of the singularity defined by f or an empty matrix if the assumptions are not fulfilled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Options: If opt=0 (default), exp(-2*pi*i*M) is a monodromy matrix of f; else only the characteristic polynomial of exp(-2*pi*i*M) coincides with the monodromy's characteristic polynomial. Display: more comments for higher printlevel. Example shows printing matrix M.

rubrics_metrics.name: H2basis Purpose / return / theory
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: H2basis(f); f poly. Assume/Return: The polynomial f in a series ring (local ordering) defines an isolated hypersurface singularity. The procedure returns a list of representatives of a C{f}-basis of the Brieskorn lattice H'' = Omega^(n+1)/df^dOmega^(n-1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theory: H'' is a free C{f}-module of rank milnor(f). Display: The procedure displays more comments for higher printlevel. Example shows basis elements returned as list entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: ArnoldAction Purpose / usage / assume
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ArnoldAction(f, [Gf, B]); poly f; list Gf, B. Purpose: compute the induced action of the stabilizer G of f on T, where T is given by the upper monomials B of the Milnor algebra of f. Assume: f is quasihomogeneous; 'Gf' is a list of two rings (coming from 'StabEqn').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: polynomial ring containing ideals 'actionid' (ideal defining induced action of Gf on T) and 'stabid' (ideal of stabilizer Gf). Example shows actionid and stabid outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: ModEqn Purpose / usage / options / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: ModEqn(f [, opt]); poly f; int opt. Purpose: compute equations of the moduli space of semiquasihomogeneous hypersurface singularity with principal part f w.r.t. right equivalence. Assume: f quasihomogeneous polynomial with an isolated singularity at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: polynomial ring (possibly simple extension) containing ideal 'modid' where 'modid' is the ideal of the moduli space if opt is even (>0); otherwise contains generators of the coordinate ring R of the moduli space (Spec(R) is the moduli space). Options: 1 compute equations of mod. space, 2 primary decomposition, 4 compute E f0; combine by adding values, default opt=7. Example shows modid entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: QuotientEquations Purpose / usage / options / assume
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: QuotientEquations(G,action,emb [, opt]); ideal G,action,emb; int opt. Purpose: compute the quotient of the variety given by the parameterization 'emb' by the linear action 'action' of the algebraic group G. Assume: 'action' is linear; G must be finite if the Reynolds operator is needed (i.e., NullCone(G,action) returns some non-invariant polys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: polynomial ring over a simple extension containing ideals 'id' and 'embedid'. 'id' contains equations of the quotient if opt=1; if opt=0 or 2, 'id' contains generators of the coordinate ring R of the quotient (Spec(R) is the quotient). 'embedid' = 0 if opt=1; else defines the equivariant embedding. Options: 1 compute equations, 2 use primary decomposition for Reynolds operator; default opt=3 (combine).

rubrics_metrics.name: StabEqn Purpose / usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: StabEqn(f); f polynomial. Purpose: compute the equations of the isometry (stabilizer) group of f. Assume: f semiquasihomogeneous polynomial with an isolated singularity at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of two rings 'S1', 'S2' where 'S1' contains equations of the stabilizer (ideal 'stabid') and 'S2' contains the action of the stabilizer (ideal 'actionid'). Global varSubsList contains substitution indices. Example shows stabid and actionid outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabEqnId Purpose / usage / assume / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: StabEqn(I, w); I ideal, w intvec. Purpose: compute the equations of the isometry group of the ideal I; each generator of I is fixed by the stabilizer. Assume: I semiquasihomogeneous ideal w.r.t. 'w' with an isolated singularity at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: list of two rings 'S1','S2' with 'S1' containing 'stabid' and 'S2' containing 'actionid'. Global varSubsList contains index j s.t. t(i) -> t(i)t(j). Example shows outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: StabOrder Purpose / usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: StabOrder(f); poly f. Purpose: compute the order of the stabilizer group of f. Assume: f quasihomogeneous polynomial with an isolated singularity at 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Return: int (order). Global: varSubsList.

rubrics_metrics.name: UpperMonomials Purpose / usage / assume / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: UpperMonomials(poly f, [intvec w]). Purpose: compute the upper monomials of the Milnor algebra of f. Assume: f is quasihomogeneous (w.r.t. w). Return: ideal listing upper monomials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example provided showing output monomials in a ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Max Purpose / usage / assume / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Max(data); intvec/list of integers. Purpose: find the maximal integer contained in 'data'. Assume: 'data' contains only integers and is not empty. Return: list (the maximum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Max(list(1,2,3)) -> 3.

rubrics_metrics.name: Min Purpose / usage / assume / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Min(data); intvec/list of integers. Purpose: find the minimal integer contained in 'data'. Assume: 'data' contains only integers and is not empty. Return: list (the minimum).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Min(intvec(1,2,3)) -> 1.

rubrics_metrics.name: codim Usage / assumptions / return / compute
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: codim(id1,id2); id1,id2 ideal or module, both must be standard bases. Return: int which is: 1) the vectorspace dimension of id1/id2 if id2 is contained in id1 and finite; 2) -1 if the dimension is infinite; 3) -2 if id2 is not contained in id1.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compute: consider Hilbert series iv1(t) and iv2(t). If codim finite, q(t)=(iv2-iv1)/(1-t)^n is rational and codimension is sum of coefficients of q(t) (n = dimension of basering). Example shows typical use. Requires standard bases; attrib(...,'isSB',1) can be used to mark.

rubrics_metrics.name: deform Usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: deform(id); id = ideal or poly. Return: matrix whose columns are kbase of infinitesimal deformations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows printing matrix T of deformation basis and usage with polynomials. No explicit assumptions beyond id type.

rubrics_metrics.name: dim_slocus Usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: dim_slocus(i); i ideal or poly. Return: dimension of singular locus of i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows computing zero-dimensional singular locus returns 0.

rubrics_metrics.name: is active (is_active) Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_active(f,id); f poly, id ideal or module. Return: 1 if f is an active element modulo id (i.e., dim(id)=dim(id+f*R^n)+1 if id submodule of R^n), else 0. The basering may be a quotient ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: regular parameters are active but not vice versa. There is a related proc is_reg to test regular parameters. Examples show usage with printlevel and different rings.

rubrics_metrics.name: is ci Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_ci(i); i ideal. Return: intvec = sequence of dimensions of ideals (j[1],...,j[k]), for k=1...size(j) where j is minimal basis of i. i is a complete intersection if last number equals nvars-size(i).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: dim(0-ideal) = -1. You may apply simplify(i,10) to delete zeros and multiples from generators. printlevel controls display of comments. Examples illustrate outputs and usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: is is (is_is) Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_is(id); id ideal or poly. Return: intvec = sequence of dimensions of singular loci of ideals generated by id[1]..id[i], k=1..size(id); dim(0-ideal) = -1; id defines an isolated singularity if last number is 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: printlevel >=0 displays comments. Examples show behavior on polynomials and ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: is reg (is_reg) Usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_reg(f,id); f poly, id ideal or module. Return: 1 if multiplication with f is injective modulo id, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Checks injectivity of multiplication with f on R^n/id. Basering may be a quotient ring. Examples show returning 0 or 1. Related procs: is_active, is_regs.

rubrics_metrics.name: is regs Usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: is_regs(i[,id]); i poly, id ideal or module (default id=0). Return: 1 if generators of i are a regular sequence modulo id, 0 otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Checks injectivity of multiplication with i[k] on R^n/id+i[1..k-1]. printlevel >=0 displays comments; >=1 displays comments during computation. Examples illustrate results and printlevel behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: locstd Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: locstd(id); id = ideal. Return: a standard basis for a local degree ordering.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Procedure homogenizes id w.r.t. a new variable @t@, computes a SB w.r.t. (dp(1),dp) and substitutes @t@ by 1. This produces a SB for a local degree ordering to avoid cancellation of units. Option(contentSB) may be used. Example demonstrates long SB output.

rubrics_metrics.name: milnor Usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: milnor(i); i ideal or poly. Return: Milnor number of i, if i is ICIS (isolated complete intersection singularity) in generic form, resp. -1 if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use proc nf_icis to put generators in generic form. printlevel >=1 displays comments. Examples show milnor outputs and printed diagnostic sequences.

rubrics_metrics.name: nf icis Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: nf_icis(i); i ideal. Return: ideal = generic linear combination of generators of i if i is an ICIS; return i if not.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This proc is useful in connection with proc milnor. printlevel >=0 displays comments. Examples illustrate genericity loop output and returned ideals.

rubrics_metrics.name: slocus Usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: slocus(i); i ideal. Return: ideal of singular locus of i. Note: Quotient rings and rings with integer coefficients are currently not supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned ideal generators for singular locus.

rubrics_metrics.name: qhspectrum Usage / assume / compute / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qhspectrum(f,w); f=poly, w=intvec. Assume: f is a weighted homogeneous isolated singularity w.r.t. the weights given by w; w must consist of as many positive integers as there are variables of the basering. Compute/Return: the spectral numbers of the w-homogeneous polynomial f, computed in a ring of characteristic 0. Return: intvec d,s1,...,su where d = w-degree(f) and si/d = i-th spectral-number(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No return value if basering has parameters or if f is not isolated; displays a warning. Example shows output encoding spectral numbers as numerator list over common denominator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tjurina Purpose / usage / assume / return / display
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: Tjurina(id[,<any>]); id=ideal or poly. Assume: id=ICIS (isolated complete intersection singularity). Return: standard basis of Tjurina-module of id, of type module if id=ideal, resp. of type ideal if id=poly. If present, a second argument may return [1] Tjurina number, [2] k-basis of miniversal deformation, [3] SB of Tjurina module, [4] Tjurina module. Display: Tjurina number if printlevel >= 0 (default). Note: Tjurina number = -1 implies id is not an ICIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show printing Tjurina number, basis of miniversal deformation, SB of Tjurina ideal, and hilbert series. printlevel controls verbose comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: tjurina Usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tjurina(id); id=ideal or poly. Assume: id=ICIS. Return: int = Tjurina number of id. Note: Tjurina number = -1 implies id is not an ICIS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows invocation returning integer Tjurina number.

rubrics_metrics.name: T 1 (T_1) Purpose / usage / return / notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: T_1(id[,<any>]); id = ideal or poly. Return: T_1(id) of type module/ideal if id is ideal/poly (the T_1-module). If a second argument present return list [1]=T_1(id), [2]=generators of normal bundle lifted to P, [3]=module of relations lifted to P. Display: k-dimension of T_1(id) if printlevel >=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: From T_1 one can obtain vdim(T_1) (Tjurina number), hilb(T_1), kbase(T_1). If called with two args, matrix([2])*(kbase([1])) represents basis of 1st order semiuniversal deformation. For CI the proc Tjurina is faster. Examples show typical printed diagnostics and use of kbase and vdim.

rubrics_metrics.name: T 2 (T_2) Purpose / usage / return / notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: T_2(id[,<any>]); id = ideal. Return: T_2(id) the T_2-module of id, a std basis of a presentation of module of obstructions of R=P/id. If a second argument present return list of [1]=T_2(id), [2]=standard basis of id, [3]=module of relations of id, [4]=presentation of syz/kos, [5]=relations of Hom P([3]/kos,R) lifted to P. Display: k-dimension of T_2(id) if printlevel >=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Most important is vdim(T_2(id)); use proc miniversal to get equations of miniversal deformation. Example demonstrates vdim and hilb outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: T 12 (T_12) Purpose / usage / return / notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: T_12(i[,any]); i = ideal. Return: T_12(i) list of 2 modules: standard basis of T_1(i) and standard basis of T_2(i). If second argument present return list of 9 objects: [1]=std basis of T_1, [2]=std basis of T_2, [3]=vdim T_1, [4]=vdim T_2, [5]=matrix presenting infinitesimal deformations, [6]=matrix of generators of relations of i, [7]=matrix presenting Hom P(syz/kos,R) lifted to P, [8]=presentation of T_1-module no std basis, [9]=presentation of T_2-module no std basis. Display: k-dimension of T_1 and T_2 if printlevel>=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Use proc miniversal from deform.lib to get miniversal deformation; the list contains all objects used by miniversal. Example shows printing L[5] and dimensions.

rubrics_metrics.name: tangentcone Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: tangentcone(id [,n]); id = ideal, n = int. Return: the tangent cone of id. Note: The procedure works for any monomial ordering. If n=0 use std w.r.t. local ordering ds, if n=1 use locstd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates returned generators of tangent cone; n controls method used for standard basis computation.

rubrics_metrics.name: isCMcod2 Purpose / usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: isCMcod2(i); i an ideal. Return: presentation matrix of i if i is Cohen-Macaulay of codimension 2; a zero matrix otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned presentation matrix for a codim-2 CM ideal.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMtype Purpose / usage / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: CMtype(i); i an ideal, CM of codimension 2. Return: Cohen-Macaulay type of i (integer) or -1 if i is not Cohen-Macaulay of codimension 2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows CMtype on simple ideal returning integer 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: matrixT1 Purpose / usage / assume / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: matrixT1(M,n); M matrix, n integer. Assume: M is a presentation matrix of an ideal i, CM of codimension 2; consider i as a family in first n variables where remaining are parameters. Return: list consisting of T1 = Mat(k,k+1;R)/K M the space of first order deformations of i, the k x (k+1) matrix M and a module K_M such that ... (provides presentation of deformations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned list structure with generators and matrices; output includes module generators and entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: semiCMcod2 Purpose / usage / assume / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: semiCMcod2(M,t1[,s]); M matrix, t1 module, s any. Assume: M is a presentation matrix of an ideal i, CM of codimension 2, and t1 is a presentation of the space of first order deformations of i (as returned by matrixT1). Return: new ring in which the ideal 'semi' describing the semiuniversal deformation of i; if optional third argument given, the perturbation matrix of semiuniversal deformation is returned instead of the ideal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Current basering should not contain variables named A(j) (internally used). Example shows semi list entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: discr Purpose / usage / assume / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: discr(sem,n); sem ideal, n integer. Assume: sem is the versal deformation of an ideal of codimension 2. The first n variables of the ring are treated as variables, others as parameters. Return: ideal describing the discriminant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: This is not a powerful algorithm. Example shows discriminant ideal A(1)*A(2)*A(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: qhmatrix Purpose / usage / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: qhmatrix(M); M a k x (k+1) matrix. Return: list consisting of an integer vector of weights of variables of basering and integer matrix giving weights of entries of M if M is quasihomogeneous; zero vector/matrix otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example shows returned weight vector and weight matrix and use of pmat(M) to display matrix entries.

rubrics_metrics.name: relweight Purpose / usage / assume / return
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: relweight(N,W,a); N matrix, W intmat, a intvec. Assume: N non-zero matrix; W integer matrix same size as N; a integer vector giving weights of variables. Return: integer max(a-weighted order(N_ij) - W_ij | all entries ij) or string "ERROR" if sizes do not match.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example demonstrates returning integer value 2 for sample inputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: posweight Purpose / usage / assume / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: posweight(M,t1,n[,s]); M matrix, t1 module, n int, s string. n=0: all deformations of non-negative weight; n=1: only non-constant deformations of non-negative weight; n=2: all deformations of positive weight. Assume: M is presentation matrix of a Cohen-Macaulay codim-2 ideal and t1 is its T1 space in matrix notation. Return: new ring containing list posw with presentation matrix for deformation given by generators of T1 of non-negative/positive weight and the weight vector for new variables.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: Current basering should not contain variables named T(i). Example shows posw[1] presentation and posw[2] weight vector.

rubrics_metrics.name: KSpencerKernel Purpose / usage / assume / return / notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: KSpencerKernel(M[,s][,v]); M matrix, s string, v intvec. Optional s names new rings prefix; optional v gives module ordering. Assume: M is a quasihomogeneous n x (n+1) matrix where n minors define an isolated space curve singularity. Return: new ring containing coefficient matrix KS representing kernel of Kodaira-Spencer map of family of non-negative deformations having given singularity as special fibre.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notes: initial basering must not contain variables e(i) or T(i). watchProgress intvec controls diagnostic/progress outputs (5 entries with described effects). Example shows complex printed diagnostics including names, weights and KS matrix blocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: spectrumnd Purpose / usage / assume / return / note
rubrics_metrics.description: Usage: spectrumnd(f[,1]); poly f. Assume: basering has characteristic 0 and local ordering; f has isolated singularity at 0 and nondegenerate principal part (second arg 1 disables test). Return: list S where ideal S[1] = spectral numbers in increasing order and intvec S[2] contains multiplicities. If second arg 1 given, no test for degenerate principal part will be done. SEE ALSO: gmssing lib.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: No return if basering has parameters or if f has non-isolated singularity; displays a warning. Example shows size of S[1] and example element with multiplicity.
